display.description:
How many volumes are attached, detached or changing state. Detached can be normal for stopped VMs and does not mean that a disk should be deleted.

Measurement details:
Sum of deduplicated 0/1 attachment-state gauges by cluster and state. Not a deletion list. Missing source metrics remain empty.
display.name: Volume count by attachment state

display.description:
Age of each non-zero last-backup timestamp. Missing data can mean no recorded backup; check the separate count above.

Measurement details:
time() minus the non-zero Unix timestamp, divided by 86400. Empty may mean no backup; see the never-backed-up tile. Does not verify target accessibility or restore.
display.name: Days since the last successful backup

display.description:
Number of backup records in each status. Completed is metadata from Longhorn; it does not verify backup accessibility or a successful restore.

Measurement details:
Longhorn 1.11.2 codes are counted and named: 0 New, 1 Pending, 2 In progress, 3 Completed, 4 Error, 5 Unknown. Zeros appear only when backup-state metrics exist.
display.name: Backup count by status

display.description: Which volumes need attention, how busy is storage, and what backups are recorded?
display.name: What this dashboard tells you

spec.text: **Which volumes need attention, how busy is storage, and what backups are recorded?** Start with volume health, then check storage space and backups. A volume is a virtual disk; this view includes all selected Longhorn volumes, including non-VM volumes. A recorded backup does not prove that a restore will succeed. **No data is not the same as zero.** Select a cluster before narrowing the next filters. **None** selects nothing; **Everything** selects all available values. After changing a cluster, reset the following filters to Everything. Full names and values opens the complete resource list. **VM / Pod** identifies a measured consumer. **PVC** means no active consumer was mapped. [Open PVCs](./#/views/urn:stackpack:kubernetes-v2:shared:query-view:persistent-volume-claims) or [Open Pods](./#/views/urn:stackpack:kubernetes-v2:shared:query-view:pods); select the same cluster and namespace, then click the resource name.

display.description:
Read and write operations per second reported by Longhorn. More activity is not automatically a problem; compare with response time.

Measurement details:
Read/write operations per second are already gauges computed by Longhorn. Do not take a second rate.
display.name: Storage read and write operations (operations/s)

display.description:
Current average response time reported by Longhorn for active volumes, in milliseconds. Compare with VM disk latency to locate storage delays.

Measurement details:
Longhorn exposes current latency gauges in nanoseconds. Divide by 1,000,000; do not apply rate(). Filter zero-IOPS volumes out because idle latency has no operational meaning.
display.name: Time to read or write a storage volume (ms)

display.description:
Provisioned logical capacity of each volume. Physical usage depends on written data, snapshots and replicas.

Measurement details:
Logical provisioned size, independent of physical bytes used and replica count.
display.name: Size assigned to each volume

display.description:
Volumes whose last successful backup timestamp is zero. Check which ones actually need backups; this includes non-VM volumes.

Measurement details:
Last successful backup timestamp equals zero. Includes all selected volumes, not just VM disks. Check which volumes require protection before scheduling backups.
display.name: Volumes with no recorded backup

display.description:
Up to 5 volumes with no successful backup timestamp. Each entry identifies the PVC and Longhorn volume; 1 means no recorded backup. Open the values table for the complete list, then compare it with your backup policy.

Measurement details:
Latest volume observations joined to the official Agent by cluster, PVC namespace and PVC name. VM identifies a running VM through the explicit kubevirt_vmi_info vmi_pod label; Pod identifies another measured consumer. The full table retains both VM and Pod names, PVC, volume and cluster. Only Running/Pending Pod labels are included. For KubeVirt hotplug disks the Agent can report the parent virt-launcher Pod; the direct mount is on its hp-volume child Pod. Association does not prove mounting or application health. PVC means no unambiguous current Pod association was measured: the VM may be stopped, the volume unused, or telemetry unavailable. Never infer a VM name from a PVC or Pod name. Shared volumes can have several consumer rows; the summary still counts unique volumes. State values of 1 mean this condition is present.

Long names are abbreviated in this panel. Open Full names and values for complete resource labels and values. The query retains the full identity; an abbreviated name alone is not a unique identifier.

display.description:
Longhorn-managed capacity, used space and reserved space on each host. Includes all volumes in the cluster, regardless of the volume filter.

Measurement details:
Longhorn-managed node capacity, used bytes and reserved bytes for other applications/system. Cluster scope: volume filter does not apply. Scheduled bytes are a different measure.
display.name: Physical storage used and available capacity

display.description:
Logical capacity scheduled for Longhorn replicas. Thin provisioning can make this exceed physical capacity; it is different from bytes already written.

Measurement details:
Logical bytes scheduled as replicas. Can exceed physical capacity with thin provisioning; do not subtract this from physical usage to calculate free disk.
display.name: Disk capacity promised to replicas

display.description:
Sum of reported snapshot sizes for each volume. Shared data and replicas mean this is not physical space usage or guaranteed reclaimable space.

Measurement details:
Sum reported snapshot sizes, deduplicated by volume/snapshot. This is not physical replicated disk usage or guaranteed reclaimable space; sharing, rebuilds and purge behavior matter.
display.name: Reported snapshot data per volume

display.description:
Volumes with a successful backup older than seven days. Compare this review window with your own recovery requirement; never-backed-up volumes appear separately.

Measurement details:
Counts only non-zero last-backup timestamps older than 7 days. Never-backed-up volumes are shown separately. The 7-day review window is not your agreed RPO.
display.name: Volumes last backed up over 7 days ago

display.description:
Volumes marked degraded or faulted by Longhorn. Open Longhorn to inspect replicas and scheduling; detached volumes with unknown health are counted separately in the health chart.

Measurement details:
Count of unique volumes with an active degraded/faulted state. Detached unknown is not counted as healthy or unhealthy here. Zero is shown only when robustness telemetry exists.
display.name: Volumes needing attention

display.description:
Preview of up to 3 affected consumer/volume entries. VM or Pod names identify measured consumers; PVC means no active consumer was mapped. The value 1 means that state is active. Check replicas in Longhorn; the full table includes every affected volume and its complete identifiers.

Measurement details:
Latest volume observations joined to the official Agent by cluster, PVC namespace and PVC name. VM identifies a running VM through the explicit kubevirt_vmi_info vmi_pod label; Pod identifies another measured consumer. The full table retains both VM and Pod names, PVC, volume and cluster. Only Running/Pending Pod labels are included. For KubeVirt hotplug disks the Agent can report the parent virt-launcher Pod; the direct mount is on its hp-volume child Pod. Association does not prove mounting or application health. PVC means no unambiguous current Pod association was measured: the VM may be stopped, the volume unused, or telemetry unavailable. Never infer a VM name from a PVC or Pod name. Shared volumes can have several consumer rows; the summary still counts unique volumes. State values of 1 mean this condition is present.

Long names are abbreviated in this panel. Open Full names and values for complete resource labels and values. The query retains the full identity; an abbreviated name alone is not a unique identifier.
display.name: Which volumes need attention?
